Ben — appreciate the detail, and great to see the MA plan. High-level response below; I attached our latest rate sheet for numbers. TL;DR: we recommend a hybrid pool (H100 for low-latency/real-time, L40S for embeddings) with a small A100 buffer for mixed workloads.

Options (examples, per-card economics in attached PDF):

1) Latency-optimized (H100 80GB) — best for 99th pctl latency at short/medium sequences
   - Use-case: real-time LLM responses, low tail latency
   - Suggested commit sizing: 16–24 cards for your 150 qps baseline (supports headroom for median payloads)
   - Throughput guidance: ~120–150 qps per 8-card shard for typical chat models (depends on model size/seq)
   - Perf/$: highest raw perf, premium price (good for customer-facing endpoints where latency is critical)

2) Balanced (A100 80GB) — flexible for mixed workloads, better memory for larger contexts
   - Use-case: mixed inference + occasional larger-context tasks
   - Suggested sizing: 8–16 cards as a shared pool
   - Perf/$: middle ground — cheaper than H100 but more expensive than L40S for simple embedding runs

3) Cost-optimized (L40S 48GB) — best for throughput and embeddings
   - Use-case: large-scale embeddings, offline batches, high token throughput per dollar
   - Suggested sizing: 24–48 cards depending on embedding volume (your 20TB/month suggests ~32-card lane to avoid long backlogs)
   - Perf/$: strongest for dense compute where memory not primary constraint

Reserved commit discounts (examples — see attached for exact numbers):
- 3-mo: ~10% off list
- 12-mo: ~18% off list
- 24-mo: ~25% off list (and improved scheduling priority during bursts)
- Additional volume tiers: +3% for commits >=48 cards

Bursting and fallbacks:
- You get a configurable burst buffer (we typically recommend 10–25% of committed capacity).
- Automatic fallback policy can route to cheaper model variants (quantized / smaller model) when committed pool saturates; we can add canary rules to prioritize important routes.

Next asks from our side to firm numbers:
- Confirm expected 95/99 pctl latency target and typical sequence length distribution (p50/p95 tokens).
- Which endpoints are latency-critical vs batch (we can map to H100 vs L40S).

I'll loop Karthik and Rishi for the formal quote and to propose a hybrid commit and pricing concession for PO timelines.

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Director, Redwood Inference

(Internal) Quick recommendation for the quote:

- Proposal: hybrid pool commit = 16 H100 cards (latency-critical), 32 L40S cards (embeddings), and 8 A100 cards as a shared buffer for larger contexts. Total 56 committed cards.
- Economic ask: offer 20% list discount for 12-mo term as base; add a 3% early-PO concession if EdgeAnalytics signs PO within 7 days of quote. This keeps margin but helps procurement.
- SLA / throughput guarantees: 99th pctl per-endpoint target of <=120ms for H100-backed routes assuming p50=80 tokens, p95=180 tokens. For embeddings lane (L40S), commit throughput to clear daily ingestion with 6–8 hour max queue.
- Burst policy: 20% immediate burst capacity; any sustained overage billed at on-demand rates, with a 4-hour automated scaling window before billing applies.

Marissa: can you draft the formal quote (numbers) and include the PO language for the early-PO concession? Rishi: can you add the SLA clause we discussed (network egress and maintenance windows) and a fallback model clause.
